asset: Wren Compressor Station · CU-2 · Dry Gas Seals
signal: Wren CU-2 dry gas seal venting more gas every hour at the same speed
aiInterpretation: Primary vent flow on CU-2's non-drive-end seal has roughly quadrupled since about 09:10, while speed, suction pressure and seal gas supply held steady. CU-1's seals, on the same gas, are flat.

detail.signal: Primary vent flow 4.70 scfm at 14:05, up from 1.37 at 09:10 (alarm 6.0, trip 8.0). CU-1 reads 1.34 scfm.
detail.observed: Rise is smooth and getting faster; seal gas filter DP up from 4.3 to 6.0 psid as more seal gas is drawn; shaft vibration steady around 1.18 mils; seal gas supply DP steady.
detail.derived: Two related signals agree (vent flow and seal gas filter DP), and the sister unit on the same gas is flat, so it is not a gas-quality or header problem. At the last half hour's rate the 6.0 scfm alarm comes in about 70 minutes.
detail.inferred: Leakage across the NDE primary seal is increasing. Possible causes include seal-face wear or contamination, or a secondary-seal problem pressurising the primary vent. Not yet confirmed.
detail.recommendation: Check secondary vent pressure and the separation-gas supply; plan a controlled swap from CU-2 to standby CU-3 before the alarm rather than waiting for a trip.

relatedOccurrences.summary: Ashby CU-1 NDE seal replaced after vent flow climbed over two weeks (contaminated seal gas after a pigging run).

detail.whatChangedSummary: No speed, seal gas or maintenance change on CU-2 today — the trend is inside the seal.

whatChanged.description: CU-2 NDE primary vent flow leaves its normal band.
Station technician confirms the vent flowmeter against the local rotameter.

detail.confidence: Two related signals agree; cause not yet confirmed
detail.risk: Medium — a seal failure trips CU-2 and vents gas; CU-3 is available as standby
detail.expectedOutcome: CU-3 in service and CU-2 seal cartridge replaced

signal: Potential-rupture alarm at MLV 1-2 — but only one transmitter saw it
aiInterpretation: MLV 1-2 pressure fell more than 10% in one scan and bounced back, several times. MLV 1-1, MLV 1-3, Harlow and Wren never moved and the line stayed in balance, so it was a failing transmitter, not a rupture.

detail.signal: MLV 1-2 read 734 psig at 10:30 while the line was near 842 psig — a 13% drop in five minutes, which meets the potential-rupture rule (10% in 15 minutes).
detail.observed: Rate of change swung between -21.6 and +28.8 psi/min. MLV 1-1 moved 2.0 psi and MLV 1-3 1.6 psi over the same window; Harlow receipts and Wren throughput were steady.
detail.derived: A real rupture draws both neighbouring valves down within minutes and opens a gap between Harlow receipts and Wren throughput. Neither happened, and the reading kept returning to the true line pressure — an intermittent signal.
detail.inferred: Intermittent open circuit in the MLV 1-2 pressure transmitter loop.
detail.recommendation: Replace the transmitter, then record the alert and the no-rupture determination in the rupture-mitigation file.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Technician found water in the transmitter conduit; transmitter replaced at 11:00.

whatChanged.description: MLV 1-2 pressure rate-of-change (potential rupture) alarm.
Gas controller checked MLV 1-1, MLV 1-3 and line balance; no pressure loss elsewhere.
Technician at MP 42: no release; water in the transmitter conduit.
Transmitter replaced and checked against a test gauge.

detail.confidence: Confirmed in the field — no release at MP 42
detail.risk: Low — a false valve closure would have cut about 900 MMscf/d of throughput

signal: Harlow receipts dropped 30% — every station downstream felt it
aiInterpretation: The Harlow processing plant's residue compressor tripped and receipts fell to about 640 MMscf/d. Wren went into recycle, then Kettle Creek and Ashby backed off in turn, and system line pack drew down before Harlow came back.

detail.signal: Harlow receipts fell from 905 to 638 MMscf/d at 08:45 and were back at 904 by 09:50.
detail.observed: Wren throughput fell to 701 MMscf/d and its recycle valves opened to 12%; Kettle Creek reached a low of 806 at 09:55 and Ashby 770 at 10:10; Segment 2 inlet pressure fell from 958 to 913 psig.
detail.derived: Each station's dip followed the one upstream by 15–30 minutes, in flow order — one cause moving downstream, not separate problems. System line pack drew down 9.8 MMscf.
detail.inferred: Receipt loss at the source: the plant confirmed a residue compressor trip.
detail.recommendation: Confirm Harlow's make-up plan with scheduling and log the receipt shortfall for the shipper.

relatedOccurrences.summary: Harlow plant power dip cut receipts for 25 minutes; Wren recycled, no downstream impact.

asset: Bexley City Gate · Regulator Run A
signal: Bexley regulator icing up — the cause was the line heater upstream
aiInterpretation: Regulator Run A's outlet gas cooled toward freezing and the regulator began to hunt. The regulator was fine: the line heater upstream had lost its flame at 10:15, so gas reached the regulators cold and the pressure cut chilled it further.

detail.signal: Run A outlet gas fell from 52.4 °F to a low of 31.8 °F around 12:00; Bexley outlet pressure swung about ±6 psi from 11:20.
detail.observed: Heater burner firing 0% from 10:15; bath temperature fell from 178 °F to 129 °F and heater outlet gas from 91 °F to 71 °F. Run B cooled in step. Inlet pressure and flow normal. Sable Ridge gas was wetter than usual from 09:30 to 11:30, but the temperature follows the heater, not the moisture.
detail.derived: The cooling started at the heater more than an hour before the regulator symptom. The regulator outlet stayed about 39 °F below the heater outlet throughout — the Joule-Thomson drop expected for a 560 psi pressure cut.
detail.inferred: Line heater flame failure (pilot out); confirmed in the field.
detail.recommendation: Relight the heater and check the flame safeguard; clear any ice from the Run A pilot before relying on it.

relatedOccurrences.summary: Tolland line heater pilot failed in a cold snap; Run B regulator froze and the monitor took over.

detail.whatChangedSummary: Heater relit at 12:10 after the flame rod was cleaned; outlet gas back above 45 °F by 12:45.

whatChanged.description: Bexley line heater flame failure (low-priority alarm).
Bexley outlet pressure deviation.
Technician finds the heater off and frost on the Run A pilot.
Flame rod cleaned; heater relit.

detail.risk: Low now — caught before the regulator froze and the monitor took over
detail.expectedOutcome: Heater firing normally; outlet gas above 45 °F

signal: Kettle Creek CU-3 shut down on high vibration — the station lost a quarter of its horsepower
aiInterpretation: CU-3 tripped at 11:52 on frame vibration high-high. Its valve-cover temperatures had started climbing about 25 minutes earlier, the usual sign of a failing compressor valve. Station throughput fell until standby CU-5 was fully loaded at 12:35.

detail.signal: CU-3 went from 239 MMscf/d to 0 at 11:52; station throughput fell from 947 to 827 MMscf/d.
detail.observed: Valve cover temperature deviation rose from 6.0 °F to 29.6 °F (11:25–11:50) and frame vibration from 0.22 to 0.93 in/s. Suction pressure rose from 750 to 772 psig as Segment 2 packed; discharge fell from 954 to 932 psig and Segment 3 line pack from 198.2 to 196.3 MMscf as it drew down. The three remaining units ran at about 85% load.
detail.derived: The valve temperature rose before the vibration did, and the engine side stayed normal — a mechanical failure inside a compressor cylinder, not an engine problem.
detail.inferred: Broken suction valve plate on cylinder 3; confirmed when the valve cap was pulled at 13:30.
detail.recommendation: Keep CU-3 locked out; replace the valve and check the cylinder and discharge bottle for fragments before restart.

relatedOccurrences.summary: CU-3 cylinder 2 discharge valve replaced after a valve temperature alarm (no trip).

detail.whatChangedSummary: CU-5 started at 12:15 and was fully loaded at 12:35; CU-3 remains down for valve replacement.

whatChanged.description: CU-3 cylinder 3 valve cover temperature starts rising.

CU-5 fully loaded; station throughput restored.
Valve cap pulled: suction valve plate broken.

detail.risk: Low now — CU-5 carries the load; no spare unit left at Kettle Creek

signal: Ashby discharge pressure swinging wider every cycle
aiInterpretation: Since 13:15 Ashby's discharge pressure has oscillated on a roughly 20-minute cycle, and each swing is larger than the last. It started soon after Ashby was held to a lower discharge limit with both units running close to minimum flow; two manual setpoint changes appear to have added to it.

detail.signal: Discharge swung between 937 and 970 psig in the last cycle; the swing was about ±6 psi at 13:20.
detail.observed: Both units' recycle valves are opening and closing in step (CU-1 up to 29%); station throughput is swinging about ±24 MMscf/d. MLV 4-1, 20 miles downstream, sees about ±5 psi.
detail.derived: The discharge-pressure controller and the two anti-surge controllers are all acting on the same flow. With the units near minimum flow, each recycle move shifts discharge pressure, which moves the discharge controller again. The manual moves at 13:20 and 13:40 landed out of phase with the swing.
detail.inferred: Hypothesis: a control-loop interaction between discharge-pressure control and anti-surge recycle, amplified by the manual moves. Not yet proven.
detail.recommendation: Stop manual setpoint moves. Put one unit on fixed base load and let the other trim, or return Ashby to suction control with the 965 psig discharge limit as an override.

relatedOccurrences.summary: Ashby discharge oscillated for 40 minutes at low flow after a unit swap; settled once one unit was base-loaded.

detail.whatChangedSummary: Discharge limit lowered to 965 psig at 12:50; units dropped below minimum flow at about 13:05; manual setpoint moves at 13:20 and 13:40.

whatChanged.description: Ashby discharge limit lowered 985 → 965 psig (Segment 4 packing).
Both units below minimum flow; anti-surge recycle valves start to open.

detail.confidence: Timing and control mode point to the loops; not yet proven

signal: Segment 4 filling up — Marlow is taking less than we send
aiInterpretation: Since 10:30 the Marlow interconnect has accepted well under its schedule, so gas built up in Segment 4 and Ashby's discharge crept toward its limit. Holding Ashby to a lower discharge limit at 12:50 stopped the build, and the segment is slowly unpacking.

detail.signal: Segment 4 line pack rose from 178.9 to 188.9 MMscf (peak at 12:55); Marlow delivery pressure rose from 824 to 893 psig; Ashby discharge reached 976 psig (limit 985, MAOP 1,000).
detail.observed: Marlow has taken about 612 MMscf/d against a 735 MMscf/d schedule since 11:00; Ashby throughput reduced from about 831 to 636 MMscf/d. Segment 4 is now 185.8 MMscf.
detail.derived: Segment 4 is unpacking at about 2.7 MMscf/h, but the gas has moved upstream rather than gone: Segment 3 gained 6.7 MMscf and the whole system 6.0 MMscf in the last hour, because receipts are unchanged.
detail.inferred: Downstream constraint: the Marlow-side pipeline posted a compressor outage at 10:40. The line will keep packing until receipts are cut to match.
detail.recommendation: Keep Ashby limited. Make sure scheduling cuts Harlow's confirmation to match Marlow's ID2 renomination (effective 16:00), and watch Kettle Creek discharge as Segment 3 packs.

asset: Sable Ridge Receipt · Moisture / H₂S Analyzer
signal: Sable Ridge gas getting wetter — heading for the 7 lb/MMscf tariff limit
aiInterpretation: Water content at the Sable Ridge receipt doubled over two hours while flow stayed on nomination, and the filter/separator started collecting liquid at the same time. That pattern points to the producer's glycol dehydrator.

detail.signal: Water content rose from 3.2 to 6.6 lb/MMscf (tariff limit 7.0) between 09:00 and 11:05.
detail.observed: Filter/separator liquid level climbed to 62%, with more frequent dumps; H₂S and hydrocarbon dew point unchanged; receipts steady at about 181 MMscf/d.
detail.derived: At its 10:00–11:00 rate the water content would have crossed 7.0 lb/MMscf around 11:30. Liquid in the separator plus rising water is the signature of glycol carry-over from a dehydrator losing circulation.
detail.inferred: Glycol circulation pump failure at the producer's contactor; confirmed by the producer.
detail.recommendation: Tell the producer the receipt will be refused as non-conforming at 7.0 lb/MMscf; send the separator liquid sample to the lab.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Producer restored glycol circulation at 11:05; water back under 3.5 lb/MMscf by 12:00.

whatChanged.description: Sable Ridge moisture warning (5 lb/MMscf).
Gas controller calls the producer; shut-in warned at 7.0 lb/MMscf.
Producer restores the glycol circulation pump.
Separator dumps accumulated liquid (sample: glycol and water).

detail.risk: Low — caught before the tariff limit; no wet gas reached a city gate
detail.expectedOutcome: Gas back in spec; lab result on the liquid sample

signal: Wren moving the same gas but burning more fuel to do it
aiInterpretation: Wren's throughput has been flat at about 905 MMscf/d since 11:30, yet its fuel keeps rising. Some of that is the higher discharge pressure as the line packs, but CU-1 is now compressing noticeably more gas than CU-2 even though they share load equally — gas is going round CU-1 without leaving the station.

detail.signal: Station fuel 3.91 MMscf/d at 14:05, up 10% from 3.54 at 11:25, at a steady throughput of 905 MMscf/d.
detail.observed: CU-1 compressor flow 512 vs CU-2 454 MMscf/d; CU-1 power 11,323 hp vs 10,058; both recycle valve commands at 0%. Compression ratio up from 1.219 to 1.233.
detail.derived: If CU-1 burned what CU-2 burns, station fuel would be about 3.72 MMscf/d — the ratio change explains that part. The other 0.19 MMscf/d matches about 57 MMscf/d circulating through CU-1, which the station throughput meter cannot see.
detail.inferred: Possible passing anti-surge recycle valve on CU-1 (seat damage or an actuator not fully closing), or a bias in CU-1's flow measurement. Not yet confirmed.
detail.recommendation: Check CU-1's recycle line temperature downstream of the valve and do an acoustic check; stroke-test the valve. If confirmed, shift load to CU-2 and CU-3 and plan the repair.
detail.whatChangedSummary: No maintenance or control change at Wren since the morning receipt cut.

whatChanged.description: CU-1 flow starts to diverge from CU-2 at equal load sharing.
Line starts packing after the Marlow restriction (raises Wren discharge pressure).

detail.confidence: The loss is real; where it goes is not yet confirmed
detail.risk: Medium — fuel lost every hour, and a passing valve erodes its seat further
detail.expectedOutcome: Recycle valve checked; CU-1 fuel back in line with CU-2

asset: Kettle Creek Compressor Station · CU-2 · Gas Engine
signal: Kettle Creek CU-2 engine detonating more and more often
aiInterpretation: CU-2's knock detection has retarded timing and shed load eight times since 11:40, and the events are getting closer together as the afternoon heats up and the station runs harder. Each clears within a few minutes, but the rate is well above this engine's normal of none or one an hour.

detail.signal: 8 detonation events since 11:40; 5 in the last hour. CU-4 had one at 12:40; CU-1 and CU-5 none.
detail.observed: CU-2 power dips about 9% at each event; jacket water and exhaust temperatures normal; ambient up from 88 °F to 93 °F; the three remaining units ran at about 85% load after CU-3 tripped.
detail.derived: Events line up with high load and rising intake-air temperature, not with fuel quality (Harlow heating value and Sable Ridge composition steady).
detail.inferred: Possible causes: warm charge air (engine aftercooler), ignition wear on some cylinders, or air/fuel ratio drift. Per-cylinder knock data is needed to narrow it down.
detail.recommendation: Pull CU-2's per-cylinder knock log; check its engine aftercooler water temperature; trim CU-2 load now that CU-5 is carrying load.

signal: Halcyon Point over-taking — imbalance will pass the OFO tolerance before a renomination can help
aiInterpretation: The plant has taken about 10 MMscf/d above its 95 MMscf/d schedule since its load ramp at 10:00. Under today's OFO the tolerance is ±1.9 MMscf. At the current rate that is reached around 15:10, but the next renomination (ID3, 17:00 deadline) does not take effect until 20:00.

detail.signal: Gas-day imbalance +1.45 MMscf at 14:05 (tolerance ±1.9), growing about 0.42 MMscf/h.
detail.observed: Delivery averaging 104.8 MMscf/d since 10:30 against a 95 MMscf/d schedule; the ID2 deadline (12:30) passed with no Halcyon renomination.
detail.derived: Time left to the tolerance: about 64 minutes. Time needed to fix it by renomination: until 20:00. The nomination route alone cannot close the gap.
detail.inferred: The shipper's nomination was not updated when the plant's dispatch was raised for the afternoon peak.
detail.recommendation: Call the shipper and the plant now: either arrange an imbalance trade or park-and-loan to cover it, or hold the take at 95 MMscf/d until 20:00. Log the call; OFO penalties apply past the tolerance.
